standard.title: Use letters and sounds to spell
standard.description: use knowledge of letters and sounds to spell words
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can write CVC words (AC9EFLY12) and have letter-sound knowledge. They have not yet been explicitly asked to apply letter-sound knowledge independently as a self-directed spelling strategy across unknown words.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can use letter-sound knowledge as a spelling strategy — making plausible attempts at unknown words by representing phonemes with appropriate graphemes.

nodes.label: Spelling is a strategy, not just memory
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can attempt to spell an unknown word by applying letter-sound knowledge — producing a plausible spelling attempt rather than random letters.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a plausible letter-sound attempt for at least one unknown word encountered in writing.
nodes.typical_width: Use knowledge of letters and sounds to make plausible spelling attempts; understand that spelling unknown words involves applying phoneme-grapheme knowledge; produce attempts where each phoneme is represented.
wider: Apply the spelling strategy to unknown topic words in different learning areas — practising transfer of the skill
Compare a plausible phonemic spelling attempt with the conventional spelling — identifying where letter-sound rules were applied correctly and where other knowledge is needed
Use the spelling strategy in independent writing tasks across different text purposes

response_modes.reason: Students may apply the spelling strategy only in explicit phonics tasks and not in independent writing. Multiple writing contexts — across different purposes and topics — help generalise the strategy so it is used independently.

success_criteria: Student makes a plausible spelling attempt — each phoneme in the word is represented by a letter.
Student uses the spelling strategy without needing to be told 'try to spell it'.
Student's spelling attempt reflects the sounds in the word, even if not conventionally correct.
